references.text: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu died when they approached the Lord's presence, illustrating the consequence of approaching the sanctuary improperly.
Any foreigner who approaches the tabernacle shall die, emphasizing the prohibition against ordinary Israelites drawing near to the sanctuary.
Aaron and his sons are to carry out the priestly service, and any foreigner who approaches shall die.
Moses, Aaron, and his sons were to camp in front of the tabernacle, and any foreigner who approached was to be put to death.
The Israelites feared dying by approaching the Lord's tabernacle, which is the direct context for the regulation in chapter 18.
The Levites must not approach the holy vessels or the altar, so that neither they nor the priests will die.
The priestly service was given to Aaron and his sons, and any foreigner who approaches shall die.
The people were forbidden to touch Mount Sinai under penalty of death, demonstrating the same principle of holy distance.
The priests had to wear the proper garments when entering the sanctuary so as not to incur guilt and die.
Only the high priest entered the Most Holy Place, and the Holy Spirit showed that the way into the sanctuary was not yet opened under the old covenant.
